newsitem.title: USA: One killed as trains collide in West Virginia.
newsitem.headline: One killed as trains collide in West Virginia.

text.p: One person was killed and hundreds evacuated from their homes after two trains, one carrying toxic chemicals, collided in Putnam County, West Virginia, emergency officials said Sunday.
The accident occurred late Saturday night while both trains were travelling on the same track, said a spokesman for the St. Albans police department.
A cargo train carrying chemicals rear-ended a cargo train hauling coal, he said. One conductor was killed but there was no information available on the victim.
Local television reports said two crew members were still missing as of Sunday morning.

The collision caused a fiery explosion, releasing chemicals including sulphuric acid and hydrogen peroxide into the air. Emergency officials evacuated hundreds of people from homes in the immediate area of the accident site as a precautionary measure.
Residents in areas further from the accident site were told to stay inside their homes.
Emergency officials said people had not yet returned to their homes as of Sunday morning, and it could be another 24 hours before the area was considered safe and people could return home.
